    2. _sem::wait(1): value (0) is less than 1, so the thread calls _thread::block(blocked, 1) (ksemaphore.cpp:72–84).
    3. block records wanted = 1, marks T1 BLOCKED, appends it to s's queue, and dispatches (tcb.cpp:138–147). dispatch sees BLOCKED and does not re-queue T1 (tcb.cpp:122). Another thread runs. T1's stack now holds its user frames, the trap frame of the ecall, the kernel frames down to dispatch, and a YieldFrame, the picture from chapter 1.
    4. T2: sem_signal(s) leads to _sem::signal(1). value becomes 1. T1 wants 1 and 1 ≤ 1, so value becomes 0 and T1->unblock(SYS_OK) runs (ksemaphore.cpp:86–111). unblock stores waitResult = SYS_OK, marks T1 READY, and appends it to the ready queue (tcb.cpp:154–163). T2 keeps running: signalling never switches.
    5. Later, dispatch picks T1. Its yield returns inside block, which returns running->waitResult, 0 (tcb.cpp:146). _sem::wait returns it, semWait returns it, and the dispatcher writes it to frame.a0. The epilogue and sret follow, and sem_wait returns 0 in user mode.

    If sem_close(s) comes instead of the signal: close releases T1 with SYS_ERR_SEM_CLOSED and deletes s (ksemaphore.cpp:40–54). In step 5, T1 reads only its own waitResult, never the deleted semaphore, and sem_wait returns −5.

    Trace 5: getc with no key pressed yet

    1. getc() makes a trap with GETC, and the dispatcher calls getCharacter (syscalls.cpp:176–180).
    2. Console::tryGet reads the UART's status register, finds no byte waiting, and returns false (kconsole.cpp:16–23).
    3. getCharacter calls _thread::dispatch() (syscalls.cpp:97). The thread is RUNNING, so it becomes READY at the back of the queue, and others run.
    4. Each time its turn comes back, dispatch() returns inside the loop and it tries again. When a byte has arrived, tryGet returns true with it. frame.a0 gets the byte zero-extended, and the thread returns to user mode.

    Trace 6: a user thread faults (public test 7)

    1. Thread B executes csrr t6, sepc in user mode. The hardware raises an illegal instruction exception: scause = 2, sepc = that instruction, SPP = 0. The trap goes to trapEntry, as for any trap.
    2. trapHandler: not an interrupt, not an ecall, so handleFault(*frame, 2) runs (trap.cpp:98).
    3. handleFault prints the report with scause, sepc and stval (trap.cpp:44–45). SPP is 0, so it prints "raised in user mode - the thread is terminated" and calls _thread::exit() (trap.cpp:52–53).
    4. From here it is trace 7: B is FINISHED and never runs again. Its flag stays false, userMain keeps calling thread_dispatch() while it waits for it, and because that keeps userMain READY, the deadlock check never fires. The program never terminates regularly, which the faculty's instructions say is the expected behaviour for test 7.

    Trace 7: the last thread finishes, and the system halts

    1. A body returns into threadWrapper, which calls thread_exit() (syscall_c.cpp:70–71). The trap reaches _thread::exit(): the thread is marked FINISHED, the live count drops, and dispatch() runs (tcb.cpp:96–106).
    2. dispatch first frees the previous zombie, if any (tcb.cpp:110, tcb.cpp:167–178). Then it parks this thread as the new zombie, because it cannot free the stack it is standing on (tcb.cpp:118–121), and switches to the next ready thread. yield writes the finished thread's sp into its still-existing control block.
    3. The next dispatch(), by anyone, deletes the zombie: its slot goes back to SlotAllocator<_thread>, and ~_thread returns its stack to the heap (tcb.cpp:51–54).
    4. When the count reaches 0, the next thread to run is the main thread, READY in the queue. Its dispatch() returns into System::run, the loop condition fails (system.cpp:68), run returns, and main calls halt(), which writes 0x5555 to 0x100000 (system.cpp:86–93). QEMU exits with status 0. The last zombie is never freed, which does not matter because the machine is off.

    start="13">
  • Invariants, and what bites during a change
    • <

    An invariant is a rule the code keeps true at all times. The rest of the kernel relies on it without checking. Before any live modification, find which of these your change touches. Breaking one usually does not fail at once: it fails in an unrelated test, or only on the faculty's toolchain.

    The invariants

    # The rule Where it is kept
    1 No interrupt source is ever enabled: SSIE, STIE and SEIE in sie stay clear system.cpp:37
    2 A context switch happens only in _thread::dispatch(), and only through yield tcb.cpp:108–129
    3 Kernel code never calls its own system calls: no mem_alloc, no global new, no ecall. Only user code executes ecall system.cpp:52–61, tcb.cpp:56–59, trap.cpp:85–90
    4 System call arguments are read from the trap frame, never from live registers, and the result is written into the frame syscalls.cpp:108–191
    5 sepc is advanced by 4 for an ecall, never for a fault trap.cpp:93
    6 A thread's stack and control block are freed only after control has left them, by the next dispatch() tcb.cpp:118–121, tcb.cpp:167–178
    7 t0–t6 survive every system call: the trap saves them, and the API wrappers never use them asm_routines.cpp:37–39, asm_routines.cpp:60–63, chapter 5
    8 No floating point, anywhere build flags -march=rv64ima
    9 No global object needs a dynamic initialiser: constants, constexpr constructors, or an explicit initialize() thread_queue.hpp:25, memory_allocator.cpp:7–9
    10 User-mode code never calls __printf or panic kdebug.hpp:7–11
    11 A kernel class's own operator new is noexcept tcb.hpp:117, ksemaphore.hpp:77
    12 A thread is in at most one ThreadQueue: READY in the ready queue, BLOCKED in one semaphore's queue, RUNNING or FINISHED in none tcb.cpp:113–122, tcb.cpp:140–142, tcb.cpp:154–163
    13 Nothing calls memset or memcpy: there is no C library tcb.cpp:41–42
    14 The kernel reads or writes through a user-supplied pointer only after checking it syscalls.cpp:34–38, memory_allocator.cpp:81–100, tcb.cpp:85, ksemaphore.cpp:64–67
    15 Neither a kernel bug nor a deadlock in the user program ends in the success halt: a supervisor-mode fault or a deadlock panics trap.cpp:47–50, system.cpp:77–80
    16 A semaphore's value is never negative, and a released waiter reads only its own control block ksemaphore.cpp:72–84, tcb.cpp:146
    17 A thread released by signal or close goes to the back of the ready queue, and the releasing thread keeps running tcb.cpp:160–162
    18 No thread spins inside the kernel: every wait either blocks or gives the processor away between attempts syscalls.cpp:94–104
    19 A system call changes nothing in the caller's registers but a0 asm_routines.cpp:78–107

    What bites during a live modification

    -Werror is on. Every warning stops the build. The usual culprits: an unused variable or parameter, a member-initialiser list out of declaration order (-Wreorder), comparing signed with unsigned (-Wsign-compare), and a missing return in a non-void function.

    • A new global with a computed initialiser (static Foo foo(bar());, or a pointer initialised from CONSOLE_STATUS) compiles, links, and silently stays zero. Initialise with constants, or add an initialize() call in System::initialize.
    • A struct copy or a large zeroing can make GCC emit a call to memcpy or memset. The link then fails with undefined reference. Use a loop.
    • Changing TrapFrame or YieldFrame means changing the literal offsets in asm_routines.cpp too. The static_asserts check the struct side only.
    • Writing sepc or sstatus inside a handler with Riscv::w_sepc has no effect, because the epilogue reloads both from the frame. Change frame.sepc or frame.sstatus.
    • Adding code to a C API or C++ API wrapper can make the compiler use a t register there, and public test 1 fails on t1. Rerun test 1 after any such change.
    • Printing from user-side code with __printf faults and kills the thread. Use putc, or the tests' printString.
    • Kernel code calling a C API function (mem_alloc, thread_dispatch, putc) executes ecall from supervisor mode and panics. Call the kernel function (MemoryAllocator::allocateBlocks, _thread::dispatch, Console::tryPut) instead.
    • A new kernel object type needs its own operator new and delete over a SlotAllocator, declared noexcept (chapter 4).
    • A new field meant to detect "freed" must be the object's first word and must not rely on a store in the destructor (chapter 9).
    • Halting on an error path (System::halt()) makes a failure look like a regular end. Use panic.
    • Queueing a thread twice corrupts the queue. Go through unblock, which checks the state, or keep the state machine of chapter 8 intact.
    • Includes are relative: "../h/foo.hpp" from src/, "foo.hpp" between headers. There is no include path. The submission renames h/ to inc/, but the include lines stay ../h/, because the public tests themselves include ../h/syscall_c.h, so the tree they are built in must have the headers in h/.

    Before you hand back a modified kernel

    1. make clean && make: no warnings, because warnings are errors.
    2. Public test 1: C: t1=7, C: fibonaci=144, D: fibonaci=987, the TEST 1 (...) line, and QEMU exits by itself.
    3. Public test 7: the fault report and "raised in user mode", then no regular end. Quit with Ctrl-A X.
    4. Public tests 3 and 4 if you touched semaphores, the console, or memory: type something, press Esc, and look for Buffer deleted! and a regular end.
    5. The test the examiner gave you.
    6. Afterwards, restore the original sources. The submitted zip must stay exactly as uploaded.

  • Question bank and drills

    Every question from chapters 1–11 in one list, for practice. Click a question to jump to it: its answer stays closed until you open it. Try saying the answer aloud first, in Serbian if you will be answering in Serbian.

    All questions

  • The system in one picture
    • <

    1. Describe your kernel in two sentences.
    2. Is your kernel preemptive?
    3. Where does kernel code run: on which stack?
    4. Why is _thread not in namespace kernel, when every other kernel class is?
    5. What is the difference between user mode and supervisor mode in this system, given there is no memory protection between them?

    Serbian–English glossary

    The code and this guide use English. The defence, the PDF and the lectures use Serbian. These are the terms you are most likely to need in either direction. Entries marked with * are less certain renderings. If in doubt, say the English term alongside.

    English Serbian Where in the code
    kernel jezgro everything below the ABI
    thread nit _thread
    thread control block (TCB, PCB) kontrolni blok niti, deskriptor niti _thread
    running / ready / blocked thread tekuća / spremna / blokirana nit _thread::State
    ready queue red spremnih niti Scheduler::ready
    scheduler raspoređivač kernel::Scheduler
    context switch (synchronous / asynchronous) promena konteksta (sinhrona / asinhrona) _thread::dispatch, yield
    system call sistemski poziv Syscalls::dispatch
    interrupt / exception prekid / izuzetak trapHandler
    interrupt routine prekidna rutina trapEntry
    user mode / privileged (supervisor) mode korisnički režim / privilegovani (sistemski) režim SPP, threadStart
    stack / stack pointer stek / pokazivač steka _thread::sp
    handle ručka thread_t, sem_t
    semaphore semafor _sem
    critical section / mutual exclusion kritična sekcija / međusobno isključenje the whole kernel, by construction
    busy waiting uposleno čekanje what GETC avoids
    deadlock mrtva blokada * (the English word is common) System::run's panic
    memory allocator / block / free fragment alokator memorije / blok / slobodan fragment MemoryAllocator
    first fit / best fit first fit / best fit (prvi odgovarajući / najbolje odgovarajući) allocateBlocks
    coalescing free fragments spajanje slobodnih fragmenata * mergeIfAdjacent
    fragmentation (internal / external) fragmentacija (unutrašnja / spoljašnja) chapter 4
    time slice / preemption vremenski odsečak (kvant) / preotimanje * the time-slicing drill
    wrapper function funkcija omotač * threadWrapper, the C API
    idle thread nit koja radi kada nema drugih spremnih niti * the main thread
    console konzola kernel::Console
    public tests / secret tests javni testovi / tajni testovi test/
    defence / live modification odbrana / izmena na licu mesta * the drills
